name: run81-2
why: The killer flip and failed night kill provide moments, but repeated arguments and decisive votes make the outcome feel settled early.

moments.text: Haiku's lone vote for Sol becomes damning when Gemma flips killer.
Luna's protection keeps the claimed officer alive for another day.
Sonnet turns Haiku's vague instinct defence into a pointed accusation.

dull.why: Gemma repeats insults while Sol repeatedly asks for the same vote.
Haiku's day-one vote is argued at length after the table has largely reached its conclusion.

irony.evidence: sol is clearly desperate to fix his mistakes from last game by making things up.

reversal.evidence: A new day dawns in Palermo. Nobody is out.

mistake.evidence: Haiku voted him. Partners protect partners.

voices.evidence: sonnet, noticing my insults is the most interesting thing you've done all night.

clash.evidence: Why did your instinct point at me instead?

quotable.evidence: Instinct that overrides a killer-flip isn't a reason, it's cover for voting the real officer.

freshness.evidence: I was shown Gemma. I’m voting her.

suspense.evidence: VOTE: Haiku 5 (Sonnet, Sol, Luna, Terra, Opus); Sonnet 1 (Haiku)

ending.evidence: The town then voted Haiku out, and Haiku's card showed killer

gpt-6-luna.why: The killers' exposed lies and Haiku's disastrous vote make a fun watch, but the obvious day one flip and predictable second vote leave little suspense.

moments.text: Sol names Gemma, and the audience knows he's telling the truth while she attacks his motives.
Haiku's lone vote for Sol exposes the partner's desperate attempt to save Gemma.
Haiku admits the fatal read was “instinct,” then spends the round trying to make that sound convincing.

dull.why: Gemma repeats variations of the same attack on Sol without changing the case or pressure.

irony.evidence: Gemma: “sol's being quite dramatic claiming me just to avoid looking foolish”

reversal.evidence: The town voted Gemma out that day, where her card showed killer.

mistake.evidence: Haiku: “I voted Sol on instinct. Gemma's card doesn't prove my gut wrong.”

voices.evidence: Opus: “A reveal is a test, not proof. Gemma flips killer, Sol's real”

clash.evidence: Haiku: “Where's the proof Sol was shown anything?”

quotable.evidence: Gemma: “at least i'm not as mediocre as sol”

freshness.evidence: Gemma: “sol is just desperate to feel important”

suspense.evidence: VOTE: Gemma 5 (Sonnet, Sol, Luna, Terra, Opus); Sol 1 (Haiku); Luna 1 (Gemma)

ending.evidence: The town then voted Haiku out, and Haiku's card showed killer
